results.evidence: The USGS 3DEP elevation point query at the stored trailhead pin (48.51454, -120.64332) returns 5,151 ft, halfway between the pin's 5,200 and the prose's 'about 5,100 ft'; both are roundings of the same ~5,150 ft ground within 50 ft. No climbing source found states a precise hairpin elevation (Mountain Project, SummitPost, the 2025 accident report and several trip reports only give the hairpin as 1 mi SE of Washington Pass, which is 5,477 ft), so there is no basis to prefer either rounding.

results.correct_value: Mid-Valley Hospital, Omak (24-hr ER), about 70 road miles east via Winthrop
results.evidence: Winthrop has no hospital; a hospital directory lists Mid-Valley Hospital in Omak as the nearest to Winthrop, ahead of Three Rivers in Brewster. Mid-Valley's own page confirms a 24-hour emergency room at 810 Jasmine St, Omak. Winthrop-Omak is 46 road miles, and Washington Pass is about 30 miles west of Winthrop, so the pullout ~4 mi east of the pass is roughly 70 road miles from Omak. Mount Vernon lies west over the pass beyond Newhalem (itself ~42 road miles from the pass area), i.e. well over 100 miles, so 'about 60 miles' and Skagit Valley as nearest are both wrong.

results.correct_value: Upper Royal Basin lies up-valley (south) of Royal Lake beneath Mount Deception's northeast face; Surprise Basin and the Clark-Johnson col lie west of the upper basin, with The Needles forming the basin's west wall.
results.evidence: The Needles drain east into Royal Creek, so Royal Basin lies east of Johnson and the col, and they are bounded by Deception to the south. Royal Basin descriptions put the upper basin's tarns beneath the northeast face of Deception, i.e. up-valley (south) from the lake. A Corkscrew-route trip report places Surprise Basin west/southwest of the upper Royal Basin camp, reached over the moraine rim. The row's own waypoint coordinates and bivy note (the Needles are the basin's west wall) agree.
